clue.text: Drunken capers caused tricky situation

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about out of order, so the following word's letters lurch into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A night of drunken antics landed someone in an awkward spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an informal word for an awkward predicament or spot of bother one gets into.

clue.text: Features East's arch-critic misrepresented

indicators.note: misrepresenting something shows it in a false shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Newspaper features by a leading critic in the East End were distorted.
explanation.definitionFit: Characteristics are distinguishing traits or qualities, which are the features of something.

clue.text: Sound broadcast endlessly before time check

indicators.note: without an end means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: audio is broadcast sound, as opposed to video
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A radio transmission runs on without stopping ahead of a time check.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection, especially of accounts, so a check.

clue.text: The final movement a student may find sentimental

indicators.note: final asks for only the closing letter of the word beside it

parts.note: its closing letter
a motion is a movement
taken as written
L, learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A music student is moved by the last movement of a symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The final movement' reads as part of a symphony, but 'final' takes just the last letter of 'The'.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional means stirred by feelings, close in sense to sentimental or tearful.

clue.text: Odds on appeal for help involving royal supporters

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so the distress call wraps around the royal letter

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the betting odds on a horse
taken as written
the international distress signal
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: A plea for help on behalf of royal patrons, with the bookmaker's odds thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odds on' looks like a betting phrase, but the odds are SP (starting price) and 'on' is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Sponsors are backers who fund or endorse a person or event, so they are its supporters.

clue.text: South bank appears insubstantial

parts.note: abbreviation for south
a bank is a lender of money

explanation.surface: A riverbank in the south looks flimsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South bank' suggests London's South Bank by the Thames, but the bank is a money lender.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means slight or small in amount, as in slender evidence, so insubstantial.

clue.text: Starts with circle and stalls

parts.note: the letter O is circle-shaped
pens and stalls are both enclosures for animals

explanation.surface: Seats in the theatre: a performance begins with the dress circle and the stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: Circle and stalls are theatre seating areas, but here they are a ring shape and animal enclosures.
explanation.definitionFit: Opens means begins, as a show opens, so the verb is a synonym of starts.

clue.text: Directed son to place for swingers, shamefaced

parts.note: abbreviation for son
golfers swing from the tee
someone shamefaced goes red

explanation.surface: A parent embarrassedly sent their son off to a swingers' venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swingers' hints at something racy, but they are golfers.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to guide the course of something, so steered means directed.

clue.text: Delegates preserve state in disarray

indicators.note: disarray is disorder, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Conference delegates try to keep the nation intact amid chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like part of the phrase 'in disarray', but it belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Representatives are people sent to act or speak for others, which is what delegates are.

clue.text: Substantial applause given by a few

parts.note: as in 'give them a big hand'
a few means some, a small number

explanation.surface: Generous applause came from only a small part of the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome sum or profit is a large, considerable one, so the adjective can mean substantial.

clue.text: Not liable for former MEP misbehaving with model

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, so ex means former

indicators.note: someone misbehaving is out of line, so the politician's letters fall out of order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
the Model T was Ford's famous early car

explanation.surface: A disgraced ex-Euro MP carrying on with a fashion model claims immunity.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exempt from a tax or duty is to be free of the obligation, so not liable for it.

clue.text: Continue heading away from explosion

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, and away says that letter departs

parts.note: a blast is an explosion

explanation.surface: Someone keeps moving, getting clear of a bomb going off.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to go on or endure over time, the verb sense of continue.

clue.text: Eastern flower samples for businesses

parts.note: a flower in crosswords is a river (it flows); the Indus is a river of South Asia
to sample something is to try it

explanation.surface: Specimens of an Oriental bloom are being collected for commercial firms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' reads as a bloom, but it is a crossword pun: a thing that flows, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Industries are branches of trade or manufacture, so businesses in a general sense.

clue.text: Illegally obtained furs worn to first night

parts.note: a stole is a fur wrap worn around the shoulders

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone wears furs to a theatre premiere, and they were acquired dishonestly.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolen goods were taken by theft, so they were obtained illegally.

clue.text: Remain, when mother leaves to bring back straw for animals

indicators.note: the familiar word for mother departs from the first word, leaving a shorter one

parts.note: taken as written
Ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the other way, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: a reed is a straw-like stalk

explanation.surface: Instructions to stay put while mum fetches straw bedding for the livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing MA from REMAIN leaves REIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Reindeer are a species of Arctic deer, so they are animals by example.

clue.text: Keen to get on up the motorway to invalid

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
an invalid under medical care is a patient

explanation.surface: Someone eager to drive north on the motorway to visit a sick relative.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; the digit 1 doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatient describes someone restless and eager for things to happen, wanting to get on with them.

clue.text: Things are confused, it's clear

indicators.note: confused things are jumbled, so the letters of the following words are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A paradox: matters are muddled even though it is obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Articles are individual objects or items, as in articles of clothing, so things.

clue.text: Letter openers individually numbered in the inventory, as listed

indicators.note: openers are the letters that begin each word, so only those are kept

parts.words: individually numbered in the inventory, as listed
parts.note: the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A clerk lists letter openers in a stock inventory, each one numbered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter openers' looks like paperknives, but it is the definition followed by the selection signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An initial is the first letter of a name or word, so it is a letter.

clue.text: Walked in a series of stages

definitions.meaning: first meaning: moved on foot, one footfall at a time
second meaning: arranged in levels or phases, like a stair

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase about walking gradually; it is two separate meanings of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of a verb for walking and an adjective for something done or built in graded phases.

clue.text: Hospital department divides to provide a sufficient amount

indicators.note: dividing something means going into its middle, so the department sits inside the other word

parts.note: to ply someone with food or drink is to provide them with it
ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A hospital department is split up so that resources go far enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty means enough or more than enough, a quantity that is ample for the need.

clue.text: When the board meant to abandon a project

indicators.note: abandoning the letter a means dropping it from the word just before

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
a signboard is a sign
taken as written

explanation.surface: The company directors intended to drop a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The board' looks like a company's directors, but it is a sign board. MEANT loses its A to give MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An assignment is a task or piece of work given out, much like a school project.

clue.text: Darkness of the spirit reflected, lacking energy

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirror-wise, so the words are read backwards
lacking something means going without it, so the physics symbol for energy is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
gin is a spirit drink
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dark night of the soul, mirrored, leaving someone drained.
explanation.walkthrough: THE GIN read backwards is NIGEHT; take out the E and NIGHT remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the dark part of the day, so it can stand for darkness itself.

clue.text: Place where it's wrong to point

indicators.note: something wrong is not right or in order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a compass point, east

explanation.surface: Somewhere one has been told it is rude to point a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or position for something, such as a building site, so a place.

clue.text: Playing here's fine

indicators.note: playing with something moves it around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A sports report: the team's performance here is good.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer fabric is very thin and delicate, which is one sense of fine, as in fine silk.

clue.text: Generous to carry the can? That's harsh

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it inside, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: a big-hearted person is generous
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Being kind enough to take the blame for someone seems unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry the can' is a British idiom for taking the blame, but here the can is simply a tin held inside another word.
explanation.definitionFit: Biting criticism or cold is sharp and cutting, so harsh in a stinging way.

clue.text: Keep quiet with book

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: A librarian's instruction to stay silent while holding a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to maintain or save it, so to keep it intact.

clue.text: Do I steal out, when friendless?

indicators.note: out can mean out of place or wrong, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A lonely person wonders whether they sneak away when they have no companions.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone isolated is cut off and alone, without company or companions.

clue.text: Drive with confidence round hotel

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: trust is confidence placed in someone
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone drives confidently around a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrust is forceful push or vigour, the noun sense of drive as energetic impetus.
